The value-extraction table (Index/t(ms) columns, virtualized rendering, live pattern preview + ignored columns), the Plot tab, value assertions, and column statistics.

## filterType merge: there is no separate "extract" filterType (this session, follow-up to `docs/archive/ui-implementation-plan.md`)

Every extraction-related feature on this page now lives on an ordinary
**`"text"` filter node** — the dedicated `filterType === "extract"` node
type, the separate "Extract" popup button (`#filterExtractBtn`), and the
two-outcome `commitFilter(asExtract)` split are all gone. A `"text"` node
whose pattern contains `[*:...]`/`[*]` wildcards is now simultaneously:

- an ordinary filter — Context/Filtered/Stacked behave exactly like any
  other `"text"` node, matched via the same `textFilterMatches`/wildcard
  code path a plain "wildcard-as-filter-shape" `"text"` node already used
  before this merge (see `evaluateFilterCondition`'s `isExtractPattern(value)`
  branch) — so the rows a wildcard `"text"` filter's Context/Filtered/
  Stacked views show are, by construction, identical to what a plain text
  filter with that same pattern would show;
- extraction-capable — `nodeHasExtractableWildcards(node)` (gated on
  `filterType === "text" && !node.isRegex && isExtractPattern(node.value) &&
  compileExtractPattern(node.value)`, previously gated on
  `filterType === "extract"`) unlocks the Table/Plot tabs for it, exactly as
  before.

**"Add filter" is the popup's only submit action now.** Typing a pattern
with wildcards and clicking it produces a `"text"` node that already has
both properties above — there is nothing left to choose between. Editing a
node's pattern to add or remove wildcards flips `nodeHasExtractableWildcards`
live on the *same* node (its `filterType` never changes), instead of the old
model where the type itself flipped between `"text"` and `"extract"`.
`ignoredColumns`/`assertions`/`columnRenames`/`plotConfig` — every
extraction-only field — are now gated on `filterType === "text"` (previously
`"extract"`) throughout every persistence carrier (`createFilterNode`/
`updateFilterNode`, `cloneSubtree`, `serializeFilterBranch`/
`importFilterJson`, `serializeFilterTreeForCache`/`materializeCachedFilters`)
— harmless to carry on a node with no wildcards, same "store it, it's unused
if not applicable" stance these fields already took before this merge.

**No migration for old `"extract"`-type data** (person said so explicitly —
no version of the software has shipped yet): `FILTER_TYPES` no longer
recognizes `"extract"` at all, so a hand-edited or pre-merge-exported filter
file/session cache/filter-library entry carrying that filterType is simply
rejected on import rather than kept loadable. Table/Plot's own tree icon/
type-tag (`TBL`) is now computed from `nodeHasExtractableWildcards(node)` on
a `"text"` node instead of a separate `filterType === "extract"` check
(`typeTagFor`/`nodeIconHTML`).

**Inversion (NOT) is no longer excluded** for an extraction-capable node —
the old `filterType === "extract"` exclusion from the tree context menu's
Invert action (alongside link/context/countContext, which stay excluded for
their own unrelated reasons) is gone: NOT on a wildcard `"text"` filter
means exactly what it always meant for a plain one — keep what the pattern
would *not* match — Table/Plot would then simply tabulate that inverted,
no-longer-wildcard-relevant result, same as picking any other filter to
extract from.

**Double-click a Table row → reveals the entry in the SAME node's Filtered
view**, not a destructive jump away (this session's accompanying follow-up
feature). `revealInFilteredView(entry, sourceEl, sourceScrollEl)` — modeled
directly on `revealInHighlightView`'s own Context-view counterpart — keeps
`state.activeId` on the extraction-capable node itself (it already has an
ordinary Filtered pane, see the filterType merge above), switches
`fhActiveTab` to `"filter"`, and selects/scrolls/flashes the row there via
the same `scrollTargetId`/`scrollTargetOffset` mechanism
`jumpToEntry` already uses.

**Click a Plot mark → reveals the entry as the corresponding Table row**
(revised 2026-09-05, person-requested — a plot click used to go straight to
Filtered too, same as the Table row's double-click; now it lands on Table
first, since that row's own double-click already goes on into Filtered from
there). `revealInTableView(entry)` stays on the same node, switches
`fhActiveTab` to `"table"`, finds the row in `extractRowsData` by entry id,
scrolls `extractScroll` to center it, and selects its cells
(`selectCells(rowCells(rowIndex))`) as the highlight — there's no
`scrollTargetId`/flash mechanism for the extraction table (unlike the log
views), so this scrolls/selects directly instead.

Both jumps replaced the old destructive `jumpToFullLog` (a jump away to the node's
root file that cleared the level filter) on their respective triggers (the
extraction table row's `dblclick` handler; the 2D `#plotSvg`/3D
`#plot3dCanvas` mark click handlers); that function has been removed.

Regression-tested: **Group 158d** (creating via the popup unlocks Table/Plot
for the same node, end-to-end) and **Group 159** (double-click on a Table
row / click on a Plot mark both reveal into the same node's Filtered view,
including the plain-click-not-a-drag case on the Plot tab). Groups
1/8/39/40/41 (fixture creation, the tree context-menu Invert exclusion, the
two-button popup redesign, column-rename persistence) were updated in place
for the merge (group-by-group detail in those groups' banners and the git
history).

## Extraction table: synthetic Index + t(ms) columns

Every extraction table leads with two synthetic columns, ahead of the pattern's own — person-requested (2026-08-17): a 0-based row-order **Index** and **t (ms)**, the *cumulative* elapsed time in ms since the extraction's first entry (0 on row 0). `INDEX_COL = -2` / `ELAPSED_COL = -1` — negative so they can never collide with `spec.columns`' dense `0..n-1` range, the same stable-`colIndex` identity scheme "Ignored columns" above already established for the pattern's own columns. Both are typed `"int"`, so they're automatically plottable/sortable/assertable/statable through every existing `colIndex`-keyed mechanism (`findExtractColumn`, `extractRowComparator`, `checkAssertion`, `computeColumnStats`, the Plot tab's axis-candidate list) with **no new code** at any of those call sites — the only places that needed to know about them at all were `renderExtractTable` (prepending the two descriptors to `extractColumns` and stamping their values) and `columnColor`.

**t(ms) is cumulative, not a row-to-row delta — a same-session correction.** It first shipped as "ΔT," the gap to the *previous* entry (blank on row 0). The person immediately flagged the design: *"deltaT macht so keinen Sinn für einen zeitlichen Plot. Der erste Eintrag müsste 0 haben, der Rest dann die bis dahin aufsummierten deltaT."* The reasoning holds up: a per-step delta can't work as a plot X value at all — row N's position on that axis would depend on the sum of every prior row's spacing, not on row N's own column value, which is exactly what a plot axis needs. Cumulative elapsed time fixes that: it's a real time axis, just relative (start = 0) rather than absolute. Renamed "t (ms)" to match, since it no longer represents a delta.

**Computation**: `values[ELAPSED_COL] = String(e.ts - entries[0].ts)` — elapsed time from the extraction's first entry, which is naturally `0` for row 0 itself (`e === entries[0]`) with no special-casing needed. Values live as **negative-index expandos on `row.values`** (`values[INDEX_COL] = String(r)` alongside it) rather than as dense array elements — every existing colIndex-keyed bracket read (`row.values[ci]`, used throughout copy/export/sort/plot/assertions) already picks these up unchanged, and `values.length` (relied on by Group 24's "matching itself is untouched" assertion) stays exactly the dense `spec.columns` count it always was, since JS arrays don't count negative-index properties toward `.length` or `.map`/`.forEach` iteration.

**Computed from the pre-sort, chronological entry order** — `entries.map((e, r) => ...)`, before `extractSortCol` is applied, and always relative to `entries[0]` regardless of any later re-sort — same as every other captured value: fixed per row at extraction time, not recomputed when the table is re-sorted by a different column. Re-sorting by Index or t(ms) itself works normally through the existing generic sort machinery.

**A third synthetic column on link pairs: Δt (ms)** (`DT_COL = -3`, 2026-09-26). When the tabulated entries are link pairs (a wildcard `text` filter under a `link` node — `entries[0].isPair`), `renderExtractTable` inserts **Δt (ms)** right after t (ms): each pair's tuple span, `pair.dtMs` (first to last real entry, see `docs/filters.md` → "Δt condition"). Chosen as the smallest fit for "analyze a link's duration": no new node type or view, the link keeps its Link view, and like Index/t(ms) the column is typed `"int"` with a negative colIndex, so sort/stats/assertions/copy/CSV and the Plot tab (e.g. X = t (ms), Y = Δt (ms) to see a drive getting slower) pick it up with no further code. Absent on a non-pair extraction. Tested: GROUP 290.

**`#btnCopySelection`/`#btnCopyAllExtract` removed (this session, person-requested)** — the two buttons that used to sit in `.extract-toolbar-row2` (now-empty `.extract-actions` wrapper removed with them) are gone from the UI. `copyTableSelection()` is unaffected — it's reachable via Ctrl+C whenever `state.tableSelection` is non-empty, independent of any button. `copyWholeExtractTable()` (copied the whole table as TSV **with a header row**, respecting ignored columns) lost its only UI trigger and has been removed as dead code; the CSV export below (`buildExtractCsv`) is the whole-table-with-header output now.

### Copying and exporting the extraction table

**Ctrl+C uses the system decimal separator, display is untouched (this session, 2026-09-02, person-reported: pasting extracted floats into Excel produced garbage because the clipboard TSV always used "." regardless of locale).** `systemDecimalSeparator()` reads it from `Intl.NumberFormat(navigator.language).formatToParts(1.1)`'s `"decimal"` part (falls back to `"."` on any error). `localizeNumericCell(value, decimalSep)` swaps a cell's `.` for that separator, but only when the cell matches a plain captured float (`/^-?\d+\.\d+$/`) — text and bare integers pass through unchanged, and nothing about how a cell is *rendered* in the table changes, only what ends up on the clipboard. `copyTableSelection` (the Ctrl+C path) runs every cell through this before joining the TSV.

**Auto-detection can be wrong — Settings → Behavior lets it be overridden (same-session fix, person-reported with a screenshot: a value pasted as `277,120` instead of `27,7120`).** `navigator.language` is the browser's UI language, not necessarily the locale the person's actual spreadsheet app parses numbers with — there's no web API for the latter, so the auto-guess can silently mismatch (a "," inserted as a decimal point gets read back as a thousands separator, shifting every digit). "Decimal separator for copy/export" (Auto/Point/Comma, `philogg-clipboard-decimal-sep` in localStorage) pins it explicitly; `resolveClipboardDecimalSeparator()` — used everywhere `systemDecimalSeparator()` used to be called directly, both the Ctrl+C path and the CSV dialog's default below — returns the stored override if one is set, otherwise falls back to the same auto-guess as before ("Auto" is simply "no override stored").

**Even the confirmed-correct separator still pasted wrong — a same-session follow-up (person-reported: pasting still broke after picking the decimal character Excel itself both types and calculates with).** Turns out the decimal character sent was never the real variable: Excel's plain-text-paste number recognition applies its own additional, unqueryable-from-a-web-page heuristics on top of whatever separator arrives, and can misfire regardless of which one is correct. The actual fix sidesteps decimal-separator guessing entirely: `copyTextToClipboard(text, html)` now writes a **second clipboard flavor**, `text/html`, alongside the plain-text TSV, via the (Chromium-only) `ClipboardItem`/`navigator.clipboard.write` API — falling back to the old `writeText`-only path wherever that API is unavailable. Every major spreadsheet app, Excel included, prefers `text/html` over `text/plain` when both are offered, and reads a numeric `<td>`'s `x:num="…"` attribute as the literal value with **no locale interpretation at all** — always period-decimal, per the MS Office HTML-clipboard spec, and exactly the mechanism Excel's own Ctrl+C already emits for numeric cells. `buildExtractClipboardHtml(rows)` builds this (`<html xmlns:x="urn:schemas-microsoft-com:office:excel">…`, one `<td x:num="raw">value</td>` per numeric cell); `extractClipboardCell(rawValue, decimalSep)` produces the shared `{value, raw, numeric}` per cell that `copyTableSelection`/`extractSelectionGrid` feed into it — `raw` (the x:num attribute) is deliberately **never** run through `localizeNumericCell`, only `value` (the visible `<td>` text and the plain-text TSV) is. Excel reads the exact value from `x:num` and formats it for display using its own locale, so — for Excel specifically — the whole decimal-separator setting above stops mattering; it remains relevant only for the plain-text fallback and other apps that read text/html but ignore x:num.

**Right-click anywhere in the extraction table → "Export as CSV…"** (`#extractContextMenu`, wired via a `contextmenu` listener on `extractHead`/`extractBody`, same open/position/outside-click-close pattern as the log table's own `#contextMenu`) opens `#csvExportDialog` — column delimiter (`,`/`;`/tab/`|`), decimal separator (`.`/`,`), an "include header row" checkbox, and an "include full log entry column" checkbox (`#csvExportFullEntryInput`, default **off**). Opening the dialog pre-fills the decimal separator from `resolveClipboardDecimalSeparator()` and pairs it with the Excel-conventional delimiter default (comma-decimal → semicolon delimiter, dot-decimal → comma delimiter) — both remain freely overridable before exporting. `buildExtractCsv(delimiter, decimalSep, includeHeaders, includeFullEntry)` builds an RFC4180-quoted CSV string (`csvQuoteField` wraps/escapes any field containing the delimiter, a `"`, or a newline; rows joined with `\r\n`), localizing numeric cells the same way the clipboard path does; when `includeFullEntry` is on, each row gets one extra trailing column ("Log entry" header) carrying that row's `entry.raw` — the entry's complete original line (timestamp, level, thread, etc., not just the message text the extraction pattern's regex matched against) — quoted through the same `csvQuoteField` as every other field. `saveCsvToFile` writes it through the shared `saveFileWithFeedback` (save picker or `<a download>`, outcome toast; see `docs/export.md` → "Saving files").

**Numeric `[*]` columns are typed** (2026-09-27, person-reported: a Patterns-view "Filter" — untyped `[*]` placeholders — showed temperature/pressure/voltage in the Table, but the Plot tab only offered Index and t (ms)). `inferNumericTextColumns()`, run by `renderExtractTable` right after `applyArrayViews`, retypes a `"text"` column (colIndex ≥ 0) to `"int"`/`"float"` when every non-empty value is a plain number (`PLAIN_NUMBER_RE`, `.` as decimal point) — so it sorts numerically and is plottable/assertable/statable like an explicit `[*:float]`. One non-numeric value keeps the column text. Only the table's `extractColumns` descriptor changes; the pattern (and its chips) is untouched. Tested: GROUP 309b.

**Plot defaults** (tablet UX round, 2026-10-03): X defaults to the **time column** (`ELAPSED_COL`; a plain-text file's Line column), not Index; with real timestamps the X ticks are clock times (`formatPlotClockTick`: `08:12:30`, `.mmm` added while the visible span is < 2 s, the date prepended when the span crosses midnight; base `extractTimeBase` = first row's ts) and the axis title reads "Time". The Y auto-pick (once per extraction, `plotConfig.yColsInit`) is the first pattern column whose values vary, float columns before int ones, constants skipped (`plotVaryingNumericColumn`); none varying → the first pattern column. A stored/user-changed choice is kept. Tested: GROUP tablet-plot-sort-context.

**Header rendering**: the numbered, colored circle badge (`.pattern-chip-num`) that marks a column's position in the pattern is skipped for `colIndex < 0` — Index/t(ms) aren't placeholders in the regex pattern, so a number there would be misleading; they still get the ordinary sort button and type tag, and (since they're plottable) are among the columns the Table toolbar's Value assertion action can target once selected (see "Value assertions" below).

**Gotcha fixed while adding this**: `columnColor(i)` used a naive `i % COLUMN_PALETTE.length`, which returns a negative result for JS's `%` on negative `i` (e.g. `-1 % 6 === -1`), indexing before the array and silently producing `undefined` → an invalid `background:undefined` inline style. Fixed to `((i % n) + n) % n`. This is exercised anywhere a negative `colIndex` reaches `columnColor` — the header swatch (moot now that the badge is skipped for negatives, but the call still happens), and, non-moot, the Plot tab's Y-column-list swatches and multi-series legend, where t(ms) can legitimately be selected as a Y series.

Regression-tested: **Group 42**, rewritten in place the same session for the cumulative correction — column descriptors/ordering, computed values (explicitly checked against what the wrong per-step value would have been), header DOM (badge presence/absence), body rendering, sorting (descending reverses order, now that every row's value is parseable — unlike the old blank-first-row delta), copy/export, the Plot tab's X/Y defaults, and the `columnColor` fix. **Group 5** targets its sort button by `data-sort-col` instead of "first one in the DOM"; **Group 24**'s column/button counts and copy-export text were bumped by the 2 new always-visible columns (its assertability check now goes through `assertableSelectedColumns()` rather than counting header buttons — see "Value assertions" above).

## Pattern restricted to columns

A wildcard `"text"` node restricted to columns (the filter popup's column chips, `node.columns`) is tabulated from those columns too: `renderExtractTable` runs the pattern against the first restricted column whose value it matches (`entryColumnValue`), the same columns `textFilterMatches` tests — otherwise against `e.message` as always. This is how a JSON Lines column (or any custom column) gets into the table: `[*]` restricted to `motor` tabulates that column's value; `[*:int]` restricted to `ctx.user` its number. Tested: GROUP 298a.

## Thousands separators in numeric placeholders

(2026-09-28, person-reported: a value logged as `1,234.5` matched `[*:float]` only up to the `,`, so every line ≥ 1000 silently dropped out of the extraction, and "Extract" split the number into `[*:int],[*:float]`.)

- **Plain `[*:float]`** also accepts a grouped number that carries **both** separators — `1,234.5` or `1.234,5` (`EXTRACT_TYPES.float`). Only that shape is unambiguous: the last separator is the decimal one. A lone `1,234` could be 1234 (en) or 1.234 (de) depending on who wrote the message, and one log can mix both, so it is never guessed. Plain `[*:int]` never accepts grouping.
- **Explicit number format**: `[*:float@en]` (`,` groups, `.` decimal), `[*:float@de]` (`.` groups, `,` decimal), same for `int` (`[*:int@en]` reads `12,345` as 12345). Grouping stays optional (`812,3` matches `@de`) but must be strict 3-digit groups (`numberFormatFragment`). The suffix goes before conditions: `[*:float@de>1000]`; condition values are always `.`-decimal. On `time`/`word`/`hex` the suffix is an invalid pattern, like a condition. It lives in the pattern string only (`column.numberFormat` is derived by `compileExtractPattern`), so no persistence carrier changed.
- **Normalized values**: `normalizeExtractedNumber(raw, col)` turns a capture into plain `1234.5` — in `renderExtractTable`'s rows and `llmExtractRows`, and inside `valueSatisfiesConditions(raw, col)` (now takes the column, not its conditions). Table, sort, plot, statistics, assertions, copy/CSV and the assistant therefore never see a separator. The pattern chip shows the format (`float@de`).
- **Auto-patterns**: `buildNumericExtractPattern` ("Extract" from a message) and the Patterns tab's `PATTERN_TOKEN_RE` treat a both-separator number as one number (→ one `[*:float]`, one Patterns group with the ungrouped values). An ambiguous `12,345` stays split; `@en`/`@de` is the explicit fix. **Constant identifiers stay literal**: "Filter for this ___", the one-click Extract and "Pair all like these…" build the pattern through `generatedEntryPattern`, which runs `freezeConstantWordCaptures` over the root file's entries — a `[*:word]` capture with exactly one distinct value across ≥ 2 matches (`v2` in `.../v2/orders/51923`) is replaced by that literal, so Table gets no constant column; the match set is unchanged, only `[*:word]` is touched, a single match leaves the pattern as is.
- Explicit literal commas still work: `[*:int],[*:int]` on `1,234` backtracks to `1` and `234`.
- Tested: GROUP 316 (sample data: log-sim's opt-in `grouped` scenario).

## Array columns

A pattern column whose every non-empty value is a JSON array (`parseArrayCell`) is an **array column** (`applyArrayViews`, run by `renderExtractTable` right after the rows are built, before sorting). Its **view** is per viewing node — `node.arrayViews: { [colIndex]: mode }`, absent = Joined, threaded wherever `plotConfig` is (gated on `nodeIsExtractionView`: `cloneSubtree`, `snapshotSubtree`/`restoreSubtree`, `serializeFilterBranch`/import, `serializeFilterTreeForCache`/`materializeCachedFilters`; `sanitizeArrayViews` keeps valid modes and at most one explode):

- **Joined** — one cell, elements joined with `", "`.
- **Per index** — one column per element, `name[0]`, `name[1]`, … (`float` when every value is a number, else `text`), up to `ARRAY_MAX_INDEX_COLUMNS` (256) — Explode and the Heatmap cover longer arrays. Each is an ordinary plottable column: Line with X = t(ms) and several `name[j]` as Y shows each element over time.
- **Aggregate** — `name.len/.min/.max/.avg/.sum` over the numeric elements.
- **Explode** — one row per element (a row with no elements stays one empty row), plus an element-index column `name #`. Only one column explodes at a time (no cross product); Index/t(ms) stay the entry's.

Derived columns carry a stable **negative** colIndex, `arrayDerivedColIndex(base, slot)` = `-(1000 × (base + 1) + slot)` (slot = element index, `900 + k` for the k-th aggregate, `990` for the element index), below the synthetic Index/t(ms)/Δt ones — so renames, sort, assertions and plot config key them like any other column, and `row.values` keeps its dense length. Every row also carries its parsed arrays, `row.arrays[colIndex]` (shared by an entry's exploded rows, which carry `arrayElem`), for the array charts below. `extractArrayColumns` lists the table's array columns (`{base, name, mode, maxLen}`).

**Switching**: a `[ ] <view> ▾` button (`.extract-array-btn`) in the first header of the group opens `#extractContextMenu` with only its four `.ctx-array-view` items; right-clicking any header of the group shows them next to Rename/Export (the current view marked active). `#extractContextMenu .ctx-item.hidden` now really hides — before, `#ctxRenameColumn` was shown even outside a header. Tested: GROUP 298b/c.

## Virtualized rendering: extraction table & Link pair view

Both views now only ever put the scrolled-into-view window (plus a small buffer) into the DOM, closing the gap noted in Known limitations ("not virtualized... would need work if someone tries to extract from an entire multi-hundred-thousand-line file with a very loose pattern"). Same underlying idea as the main log table's `renderVisibleRows`/`#tableSpacer`/`#tableRows`, adapted to each view's own DOM shape.

**Extraction table** (`renderExtractVisibleRows`): `extractRowsData`/`extractColumns` always hold the FULL result — sort, cell selection, copy/export, column statistics, and the Plot tab all keep operating on the complete set exactly as before, completely unaffected by virtualization. Only the row-building loop that used to run once per `renderExtractTable()` call moved into its own function, keyed off a fixed `EXTRACT_ROW_HEIGHT` (28px, enforced via an inline `style.height` on every `<tr>`, same reasoning as the main table's `ROW_HEIGHT`) and a `EXTRACT_BUFFER_ROWS` (15) buffer above/below the viewport. Because `#extractHead`/`#extractBody` are a real `<table>` (needed for the sticky header + sticky gutter column + native cell borders the existing UI already relies on), the windowed subset can't be absolutely-positioned the way `#tableRows` is — instead **two spacer `<tr>`s** (a single `<td colspan>` each, sized via inline `height`/`padding:0`/`border:none` so no dedicated CSS rule is needed) stand in for the rows above/below the rendered window, keeping the scrollbar's range correct. `#extractHead` is itself NOT virtualized (one sticky row, always fully rendered) but its own rendered height still occupies scroll-flow space above row 0 (sticky positioning doesn't remove it from layout) — `extractHead.offsetHeight` is read directly and subtracted from `extractScroll.scrollTop` wherever the body's own scroll offset is computed, rather than assuming the header takes 0px. `applyExtractSelectionClasses()` now runs at the end of every windowed re-render (not just the initial full build), so a selection made before scrolling still shows `.cell-selected` correctly on whatever happens to scroll into view later. Switching to a different extraction node now also resets `extractScroll.scrollTop` to 0 — needed once virtualization exists (a stale deep scroll position into a much smaller new result would otherwise render starting mid-air, or entirely past the new table's own end); this was a latent gap before virtualization too, just invisible since every row always had a DOM node regardless of scroll position.

**Link pair view** (`renderLinkVisibleBlocks`): a pair-block's height varies with its tuple size (`getTupleEntries(pair).length` — 2 rows/1 delta for a plain link, N rows/N-1 deltas for a chained/multi-hop tuple, see "Link filter" above), so unlike the two fixed-row-height table views this can't just divide `scrollTop` by a constant. `computeLinkBlockOffsets()` builds a prefix-sum array (`linkBlockOffsets`, length `linkPairsData.length + 1`) analytically from each block's real-entry count via `linkBlockHeight(n) = n·LINK_PAIR_ROW_HEIGHT + (n-1)·LINK_DELTA_HEIGHT + (2n-2)·LINK_ROWS_GAP + LINK_BLOCK_MARGIN` — the exact same constants (`.pair-row`/`.pair-delta` heights now enforced via inline `style.height`, `.pair-rows`' own flex `gap`, `.pair-block`'s `margin-bottom`) the CSS already used, just made exact instead of left to natural layout, so the formula's output is guaranteed correct with no DOM measurement needed. `linkBlockIndexAtOffset()` binary-searches that array to find which block a given pixel offset falls into. The rendered window is buffered in **pixels** (`LINK_BUFFER_PX = 300`), not a row/block count, since blocks aren't uniform height. `#linkBody` moved from a plain block-flow container to the same `#linkSpacer`(`position:relative`, full height)/`#linkBody`(`position:absolute`, offset via inline `top`) split `#tableSpacer`/`#tableRows` already established, since (unlike the extraction table) it's plain `<div>`s, not a native `<table>`, so absolute positioning works directly — no spacer-row workaround needed here.

**Pair selection had to stop being DOM-class-only.** Before virtualization, `.pair-block` for every pair always had a live DOM node, so "which pair is selected" could just be read back off whichever element currently carried `.pair-selected` (`linkBody.querySelector(".pair-selected .pair-brace")`). Once a block can be torn down and rebuilt between a click and any later read (scrolled away, then back), that stops being a safe source of truth — a selection made, then scrolled out of view, would silently vanish the instant the block left the DOM, and `minimapMarkedEntries()` (which used exactly that query) would incorrectly report nothing marked. Fixed by tracking selection as `linkSelectedPairIndex` (an index into `linkPairsData`, not a DOM reference) — `applyLinkSelectionClasses()` re-applies `.pair-selected` to whichever *currently-rendered* block matches that index after every windowed re-render, and `minimapMarkedEntries()`/`applySelection()` (the "a plain row selection supersedes a stale Klammer" clearing logic) both read/write the index directly instead of touching `linkBody` at all. A side effect, not a regression: pair selection now also **persists across a re-render of the same link node** (e.g. toggling a level filter) — previously any full `renderLinkView()` rebuild silently dropped the selection since the DOM class had no state to survive the rebuild; now it does, matching how `state.tableSelection`/`state.selectedId` already behave elsewhere. Switching to a genuinely *different* link node still resets both the scroll position and `linkSelectedPairIndex` (`renderLinkView`'s `linkNodeId !== node.id` check, same pattern `renderExtractTable`'s `extractNodeId` check already used).

The minimap's own "rendered subset" sub-rectangle stays deliberately hidden for the Link view (unaffected by this work) — extending it to the Link view's own (differently-shaped) virtualization wasn't part of what this item asked for. `updateMinimapRenderedRange` enforces this with its own explicit guard (`linkWrap.style.display !== "none"`) rather than by simply never being called during the Link view — see "Timeline minimap" in `docs/filters.md` for the later session that made that guard necessary (the Context view now keeps rendering in the background even while the Link view is on screen).

Regression-tested: **Group 45** in `tests/philogg.regression.test.js` — extraction table: windowed DOM row count bounded well below a 300-row result, correct top/bottom spacer heights before and after scrolling, select-all still covering every logical cell (not just the rendered subset), a rendered cell correctly showing `.cell-selected` after a windowed re-render, and scroll resetting on a node switch; Link view: `linkPairsData`/`linkBlockOffsets` always reflecting the full 50-pair result regardless of what's rendered, a bounded rendered block count, the render window actually moving to a deterministically-computed block index on scroll, a pair selected then scrolled fully out of view keeping no stale `.pair-selected` anywhere while `minimapMarkedEntries()` still resolves it correctly, `.pair-selected` correctly reappearing once scrolled back, and both scroll position and selection resetting on a genuine node switch.

**Panel-resizer drag handlers now rAF-batch their re-render too** (code-review finding, 2026-08-18): every high-frequency scroll listener above already collapses rapid events onto `requestAnimationFrame` via a `xTicking` boolean guard — `tableBody`/`highlightBody`/`extractScroll`/`linkScroll`'s `"scroll"` listeners all follow this shape. The three panel-resize drag handlers (`#detailResizer`, `#sidebarResizer`, `#fhSplitResizer` — see "Header / toolbar layout"/"Context view" for what each resizes) had been missed: their `mousemove` handlers called `renderVisibleRows()`/`renderHighlightVisibleRows()`/`renderTimelineMinimap()` synchronously on every raw event. `mousemove` fires far more often than the display repaints, so a fast drag reran that work (for the sidebar case, two full row-window rebuilds *plus* a full timeline-minimap SVG rebuild — the overlay pass is O(current view size) even with the background pass memoized, see "Known limitations") once per input event instead of once per frame — visible stutter on a large filtered view. Fixed with the exact same `xTicking`/`requestAnimationFrame` guard the scroll listeners already use per handler (`detailResizeTicking`/`sidebarResizeTicking`/`fhResizeTicking`); the geometry write itself (`style.width`/`style.height`, what makes the panel visibly track the cursor) stays **outside** the throttle so there's no added input latency — only the expensive re-render is deferred and collapsed. Regression-tested: **Group 47** — for each of the three resizers, dispatching several rapid `mousemove` events confirms the style geometry updates synchronously on every one while the re-render function stays uncalled until a `setTimeout` lets the batched `requestAnimationFrame` actually fire, at which point it's been called exactly once despite the multiple input events.

## Plotting (inside the extraction table's Plot tab)

Custom SVG chart builder, no library. Line / Bar / Scatter / 3D scatter, plus the value charts Heatmap / Profile / Radar / Parallel coordinates (see "Value charts" below), chosen per-plot via `plotConfig` (3D renders to a `<canvas>` instead of the SVG — see "3D scatter" below). Only columns with a numeric-capable type (`isPlottableType`: `float`/`int`/`hex`/`time`) are offered as axis candidates; `time` values are parsed to milliseconds (`parseTimeToMs`) so time columns are plottable too.

- **Chart type row** (`#plotTypeRow`, Line/Bar/Scatter/3D/Heatmap/Profile/Radar/Parallel, `.plot-type-btn`, wrapping four per row via `min-width: calc((100% - 15px) / 4)`): all eight are `flex:1 1 0` — a **zero** flex-basis, not the `auto` every other flex row in the app uses — so they split the row exactly evenly regardless of label length (this session, 2026-09-15, person-reported: `flex:1 1 auto` sizes each button off its OWN content first, so "Scatter" rendered visibly wider than "3D" despite identical `flex-grow`; a zero basis ignores content width entirely, buttons become pixel-identical).
- **Line/Bar**: multi-select Y columns (checkboxes, colored to match their extraction-table chip); line points are connected in **row order**, not sorted by X value, because extracted rows are already in the log's chronological order and that's almost always the meaningful sequence.
- **Scatter**: single X, single Y, optional third **color-by-value** column rendered with a colormap gradient (`plotColorScale`) plus a legend. A **Colormap** dropdown (`#plotColorMapSelect`, `plotConfig.colorMap`) picks which one — `PLOT_COLOR_MAPS` (default blue→yellow→red, plus Viridis/Plasma/Cool–Warm/Grayscale/Turbo); default stays the pre-existing blue→yellow→red scale, so nothing changes for a plot that never touches the picker. Shown only while "Color by" is set to something other than None (person-requested follow-up, same session: showing it unconditionally implied it did something even with no color-by column active) — `renderPlotControls` builds it as an empty string when `plotConfig.colorCol == null`, and `#plotColorSelect`'s own change handler now calls `renderPlotControls()` (not just `renderPlotChart()`) so the picker appears/disappears immediately as Color by is set/cleared; the underlying `plotConfig.colorMap` choice itself is untouched while hidden, same as any other plotConfig field. Shared by 2D scatter and 3D (same `plotColorScale(t, plotConfig.colorMap)` call, see "3D scatter" below).
- **Axis scaling**: `niceTicks()` is a standard "nice numbers" algorithm (picks a 1/2/5×10ⁿ step) so tick spacing looks sensible regardless of whether the data is in the hundreds (mm) or 10⁻⁵ range (µm) — this was a specific requirement, not an afterthought. Manual min/max override inputs exist per axis for when auto isn't wanted. For comparing multiple Y-series that live on very different scales in the *same* chart, there's a **"Normalize each series (0–1)"** toggle (only shown with 2+ series selected) — auto-scaling alone can't fix that case since it's one shared axis across series.
- **Gotcha already hit and fixed**: don't auto-refill an "empty" multi-select (Y columns) on every re-render — it fights the natural "uncheck the old one, check the new one" interaction, since the render in between the two clicks sees zero-selected and silently restores a default. Fixed by only auto-picking Y defaults once per extraction (`plotConfig.yColsInit`), not every render.
- **Bugfix: tailing was silently closing an open axis dropdown** (this session, 2026-08-19, person-reported: *"während ein Log im Tailing ist, kann ich die Plots nicht korrekt Bedienen. wenn ich das dropdown zur Auswahl einer Datenspalte für z. B die x Werte öffne, schließt es sich kurz darauf von selbst."*). `renderExtractTable()` calls `renderPlotControls()` unconditionally whenever the Plot tab is open — including from `onTailChange()`'s plain `render()`, which fires on every tail poll tick while a file is actively being written to. `renderPlotControls()` did a flat `plotControls.innerHTML = html`, tearing down and recreating `#plotXSelect`/`#plotYSelectSingle`/etc. on every one of those calls — a real browser closes an open native `<select>` the instant its element is removed from the document, which is exactly what a tail tick was doing mid-interaction. This is the same class of DOM-identity bug CLAUDE.md's "Known gotchas" already documents for `renderVisibleRows()`/native `dblclick` and `renderTree()`/native `click` during a load tick — just for `<select>`/native dropdown-open state this time. The wasted rebuild itself was also just wrong on the merits: tailing only ever appends **row** data (`extractRowsData`); it never touches the pattern/columns/`plotConfig` the controls' HTML is actually built from, so the DOM never needed to change in the first place. Fixed with a content-diff guard: `html` (the string about to be written) is a pure function of `extractColumns`/`plotConfig`, so comparing it against `lastPlotControlsHtml` (the string from the last real write) is a simple, general "would this rebuild actually change anything" check — identical means skip the `innerHTML` write (and the listener re-attachment right after it, which only makes sense paired with fresh nodes) entirely, leaving whatever's currently open alone. `loadPlotConfigForNode()` clears `lastPlotControlsHtml` too, so a genuine node switch always forces one real rebuild regardless of any coincidental string match. The chart itself (`renderPlotChart()`) is untouched by this and keeps updating live every tick, as it should — only the controls' own DOM churn is guarded. Regression-tested: new **Group 62** — a real `tailTick()` (fake `FileSystemFileHandle`, same technique Group 12 uses) that adds a new extraction row asserts both axis `<select>` elements are the SAME DOM node afterward (not recreated) while the chart's own mark count DID grow to 4; a second, empty tick is equally inert; and a genuine control change (chart type Line→Bar) still produces a new node, proving the guard doesn't suppress real updates.
- **Point/bar → log entry** (this session, 2026-08-18, from `FEATURE_BACKLOG.md`'s "Plot point → log entry" — the Plot tab used to be a dead end, an outlier visible but not reachable): every mark (line/scatter point circle, bar rect — not the assert-violation ring drawn on top of a flagged one) carries `class="plot-mark" data-row="<index into extractRowsData>"` (`p.rowIndex`, already computed for bar's group positioning, reused here). One delegated `click` listener on `#plotSvg` (not per-mark — `renderPlotChart` rebuilds the SVG's `innerHTML` wholesale every render) resolves `ev.target.closest(".plot-mark")` back to `extractRowsData[row].entry` and calls **`revealInTableView`** (revised 2026-09-05, person-requested — see "filterType merge" at the top of this doc for the original follow-up feature this replaced; previously the (since removed) `jumpToFullLog`, before an extraction-capable node had a Filtered view of its own to reveal into, then `revealInFilteredView` straight to Filtered, now `revealInTableView` to the Table row first). Clicking chart background/axes/gridlines (no mark under the cursor) is a no-op. `.plot-mark{cursor:pointer}` + a `:hover{opacity:.7}` dim are the only visual affordance — no per-mark tooltip, kept deliberately minimal.
- **Equal axis scale** (`plotConfig.axisEqual`, this session, 2026-08-18, from `FEATURE_BACKLOG.md`'s "Axis-Equal" suggestion): a checkbox (`#plotAxisEqual`, default off, hidden for Bar — its X is categorical/one-bar-per-row, so a pixel-per-unit ratio doesn't apply) that keeps X and Y at the same pixel-per-data-unit ratio, so a plot of two same-unit quantities (the motivating case: `Position x=[*:float] y=[*:float]`) isn't visually stretched by the chart area's own aspect ratio. Implementation stays a pure presentation-layer step, deliberately not touching `niceTicks`' output: after the home domain's ticks are computed as usual, whichever axis has the smaller data-units-per-pixel (i.e. the *looser* one — more screen space than it strictly needs) gets its **pixel-mapping domain** (`xHomeDomainMin/Max`/`yHomeDomainMin/Max`, separate from the tick-generating min/max) symmetrically padded until both axes' ratios match; the tighter axis is left untouched. Ticks/gridlines still render at their original "nice" values and positions — the padding only ever adds blank margin beyond the data, it never re-buckets the ticks themselves. `normalize`/`xMin` etc. live on `plotConfig` like every other axis setting — see "Plot config persists per extraction node" below for how that's actually persisted (only the zoom/pan *viewport* stays ephemeral).

### Column names, units and role chips (2026-09-29, person-requested)

**Names and units.** Extraction columns are named after the message text right before their placeholder, with a short unit word after it as `col.unit` — rules in `docs/filters.md` (placeholders paragraph). Tuple-style messages (`(xo, yo, zo): (1.4, 7.98, 9.76)` and variants, group units like `[mm]`) pair a name list with the value list positionally (`deriveTupleNames`). `columnAxisLabel(col)` (`name [unit]`) is used for the 2D X title, the single-series Y title, the heatmap/profile X title, the scatter color-bar title and the 3D axis labels; legends, table headers, select options and stats keep the plain name. The sidebar Y list shows the name in normal case (`.plot-field label.plot-y-item`) plus a dim `.plot-y-unit`. `#extractPatternView` chips show the display name plus a dim `.pattern-chip-sub` (unit, else type@fmt), the condition label appended.

**Role chips (Plot tab only).** While `extractView === "plot"` and something is plottable, `renderExtractPatternView` prepends a `Row` group (chips for Index `#`, t (ms) `t`, Δt (ms) `Δ` on link pairs) and a `Message` label, and gives every plottable chip a badge area: X/Y/Z/C for line/bar/scatter/3D (`Y` on scatter/3D = `yCols[0]` only), the 1-based `multiCols` position for radar/parallel and heatmap/profile in column mode (plus heatmap X, parallel C), `V` on the array column in array mode; a dashed `+` for a plottable chip without a role, nothing for word/text/ignored chips. A click (`stopPropagation`) opens `#plotRoleMenu` — one body-level element styled like `#extractContextMenu`, keyed by colIndex so a tail tick's pattern-view rebuild doesn't close it; closes on outside click, Escape, an item, Table tab, node switch. Items: X/Y (add/remove on line/bar)/Z/Color by/Add-Remove from columns/Values/Not plotted, then Ignore/Include column (pattern chips only — the Table tab's click-to-ignore is unchanged there). "Not plotted" is disabled where the role can't be empty (X; Y/Z on scatter/3D; heatmap X; array V). Every change goes through `setPlotColumnRole(role, ci)`, which mutates `plotConfig` like the sidebar controls; `renderPlotChart` calls `refreshPlotRoleBadges()` so badges follow sidebar edits. `switchExtractView` rebuilds the pattern view from `lastPatternViewArgs`. The 2D X title, single-series Y title and scatter color-bar title are `.plot-axis-clickable` (`data-axis`, a separate `.plot-axis-caret` ▾ so the title text stays exact) and open a column menu through the same path. `renderPlotControls`' unchanged-HTML cache key includes the role fields, so the sidebar selects follow outside changes. Derived array columns (`bins[1]`) have no chip — sidebar only. Drag & drop onto the chart stays in `FEATURE_BACKLOG.md` #74.

Regression-tested: **Group 325** (naming/unit rules, chip text, axis titles, rename keeps unit, Y list), **Group 327** (tuple names and group units, end to end on the simulator's `tuples` scenario), **Group 326** (badges per chart type, menu actions, sidebar sync, Table tab unchanged, menu survives a re-render, axis-title menu).

### Value charts: Heatmap, Profile, Radar, Parallel coordinates

Four chart types (`PLOT_VALUE_CHART_TYPES`, `isValueChartType`) that plot a **vector of numbers per table row** instead of one X/Y pair. `valueChartSource()` supplies the vectors (`{ rows: [{ r, a }], cols, label, … }`) from one of two sources:

- **An array column** — Heatmap/Profile only, picked in `#plotArraySelect` ("Values"; `plotConfig.arrayCol`, the column's base colIndex, with `plotConfig.arraySource = "array"`). Reads `row.arrays` whatever the column's table view is; an exploded entry counts once.
- **A column group** — `plotConfig.multiCols`, an ordered list of plottable colIndexes, edited in `#plotColList` (checkbox per plottable column, ▲/▼ to reorder; the order is the axis/spoke/element order). Radar and Parallel always use it; Heatmap/Profile when "Columns" is chosen in the Values select (`arraySource = "columns"`) or the table has no array column. Picked once by default (`multiColsInit`): the pattern's own numeric columns (colIndex ≥ 0), up to 8. A row counts when at least one of its values is a number.

All four render into `#plotSvg` without zoom/pan (`plotLastRender` stays null, which hides the 2D zoom tools); every cell/point/line is a `.plot-mark` (click → `revealInTableView`) with a `<title>` tooltip.

- **Heatmap** — X = a plottable column (`plotConfig.xCol`; switching to Heatmap from the Index default picks t(ms)), Y = element index or column (labelled with column names when each band is ≥12px), color = value through `plotConfig.colorMap`, with a colorbar. One color scale for all values, so it is meant for same-unit data (array elements, `ch0…chN`). Rows are sorted by X; each gets a band reaching halfway to its neighbours. More rows (or elements) than one per `PLOT_ARRAY_MIN_BAND_PX` (2px) are averaged in consecutive groups (`groupEvenly`), so the number of rects is bounded by the chart's size, not by the log's.
- **Profile** — X = element index or column, Y = value for one row: `#plotProfileRow` slider (`plotConfig.profileRow`, default the last row), plus up to 8 rows selected in the Table tab (`state.tableSelection`, `valueChartOverlays`) as overlays. One Y scale spanning every row, so it stays put while sliding — again same-unit data.
- **Radar** — one spoke per column (≥3), each scaled to **its own** min..max over all rows (minimum at `PLOT_RADAR_INNER` = 12% of the radius, so a row at every minimum is still a visible polygon), labelled with the column name and its range. Same row slider and Table-selection overlays as Profile. The one for mixed units (temperature/pressure/voltage): a single row against the normal state at a glance. Shape and area depend on the spoke order — that's what ▲/▼ are for.
- **Parallel coordinates** — one vertical axis per column (≥2), each on its own nice-ticked scale, one `<path class="plot-pc-line">` per row, broken at a non-numeric value. Optional **Color by** (`plotConfig.colorCol`, shared with Scatter) through the colormap, with a colorbar. More rows than `PLOT_PARALLEL_MAX_LINES` (3000) are drawn evenly sampled (every k-th row; the info line says so) — counts and selection still cover every row.
  - **Axis brush**: a transparent `.plot-pc-axis-hit` strip on each axis; left-drag along it sets that column's range (`plotParallelBrushes`: colIndex → [lo, hi] in data units, from `plotParallelLayout`'s axis geometry, rAF-batched re-render while dragging), a plain click clears it. Rows outside any range get `.plot-pc-dim` and are drawn underneath. `#plotBrushInfo` shows "n of N rows in range"; **Select in table** (`selectParallelBrushedRows`) selects those rows' cells and switches to the Table tab; **Clear ranges** drops all. The ranges are viewport state like `plotZoom`: not persisted, reset by `loadPlotConfigForNode`, removed for a column taken out of the group.

`arrayCol`/`profileRow`/`arraySource`/`multiCols`/`multiColsInit` are `plotConfig` fields (sanitized like the others: `arraySource` ∈ array/columns, `multiCols` integers, deduplicated). The assistant's `show_view` tool sets all of these too (`plot.columns`/`array`/`row`/`ranges`, see `docs/llm-assistant.md`); an open range end from it (±Infinity) is drawn clamped to the axis. Tested: GROUP 299 (array source), GROUP 310 (column group, Radar, Parallel, brush), GROUP 311 (assistant).

### 3D scatter (this session, 2026-08-28, person-requested — previously deferred)

A fourth chart type, `plotConfig.type === "3d"`. Unlike Line/Bar/Scatter, it does **not** render into `#plotSvg` — there's a dedicated `<canvas id="plot3dCanvas">` sibling of `#plotSvg` inside `#plotChartArea`, and `renderPlotChart()` branches to `renderPlot3D()` at the very top, toggling `.hidden` on whichever of the two isn't the current chart type. No 3D library — hand-rolled orthographic projection (`project3dPoint()`): a point is rotated by yaw (`plot3dView.rotY`, around the world-Y axis) then pitch (`plot3dView.rotX`, around the resulting X axis, clamped to ±~89° so the view can't flip through straight up/down), then projected by simply dropping Z (used only for depth-sort via a painter's algorithm and read back as `depth`), and finally scaled/panned by `plot3dView.zoom`/`panX`/`panY`. Good enough for a scatter of points; nowhere near a full 3D engine (no lighting, no perspective divide, no occlusion beyond draw order).

- **Axis selection**: X/Y/Z each a single-select dropdown (`#plotXSelect`/`#plotYSelectSingle`/`#plotZSelect` — Y and Z reuse `plotConfig.yCols[0]`/`plotConfig.zCol`), plus the same optional color-by column, colormap picker, and gradient/legend as 2D scatter. The 2D-only controls (multi-Y checkboxes, normalize toggle, the single `axisEqual` checkbox) are hidden for this chart type — the manual range inputs stay, see below.
- **Colorbar height matches 2D's** (person-requested, 2026-09-16: *"Die colormap der 2D Plots erstreckt sich über die gesamte Fensterhöhe. Beim 3D Plot ist die Leiste deutlich kleiner. Gleiche die Darstellung in 3D an die der 2D Plots an."*). The legend strip in `renderPlot3D()` used to cap at `Math.min(140, cssH - 32)` — visibly shorter than 2D's, which always spans the full plot height (`legendH = plotH`). Fixed by dropping the 140px cap (`legendH = Math.max(20, cssH - 32)`), so it now spans the chart area's height the same way 2D's does, just measured against the canvas instead of the SVG plot rect. The canvas `CanvasGradient` also gained more color stops (10, up from a hardcoded 3) so a mid-length colormap like Viridis or Turbo reads correctly in the gradient, not just at its 0/50/100% points.
- **Manual axis ranges** (`plotConfig.xMin/xMax/yMin/yMax` — same fields 2D's own X/Y range inputs write, since the two chart types never render controls at the same time — plus new `zMin`/`zMax`), person-requested same-session follow-up: `#plotXMin`/`#plotXMax`/`#plotYMin`/`#plotYMax`/`#plotZMin`/`#plotZMax`, "auto unless overridden" exactly like 2D — empty means "use the data's own min/max for that axis." Each is a shared `.stepper` pill (this session, 2026-09-15's UI harmonization — see `docs/ui-and-views.md` → "Shared 'stepper' control") rather than a bare native number spinner: `renderPlotControls` builds the pair via `stepperInputHtml(id, {placeholder:"auto", value, compact:true})` on every rebuild, and the `rangeIds.forEach` loop right after wires the existing `"change"` listener AND `initNumberStepper(id, {step:1})` for the new Dec/Inc buttons — both drive the exact same `plotConfig[key] = ev.target.value` write, so typing and clicking stay indistinguishable to the rest of the pipeline. **`compact:true`, plus `#plotControls` itself widening `220px → 250px`, are both same-session follow-ups (person-reported via screenshot: two full-size steppers side by side didn't fit — the second one's own +/- buttons were pushed off the sidebar's visible edge)**: the default (non-compact) stepper needs `2*(32+44+32)+6 = 226px` for a range pair, more than the old sidebar ever had free; the range fields now use `.stepper-compact` (the same `26px`-button/`38px`-value size the toolbar zoom controls use) with the wider sidebar as additional headroom. Used in `renderPlot3D()` as the extent each axis is centered/scaled from (`xLo`/`xHi`/etc., analogous to 2D's `xRawLo`/`xRawHi`) — a manual range changes what world-scale `1/range` that axis gets (and therefore feeds into `axisEqual3d`'s "tightest scale wins" comparison below), not a point filter: a point outside the chosen range still renders, just off-center/off-scale, since 3D has no clip-path the way the 2D SVG chart's `<clipPath id="plotClip">` does.
- **Equal axis scale** (`plotConfig.axisEqual3d`): a select, not a checkbox, since three axes admit more combinations than 2D's binary in/out — `"off"` (each axis independently normalized to fill the view), `"all"` (X=Y=Z), or any one pair equal with the third auto (`"xy"`/`"xz"`/`"yz"`). Implementation: each axis gets an independent world-scale `1/range`; for a tied group, all its axes are set to the **smallest** individual scale in that group (the tightest/least-stretched one) — same "the tighter axis wins, the looser one gets padding" reasoning as 2D's `axisEqual`, just expressed as a world-unit scale factor (in a cube coordinate space) instead of a pixel-mapping domain pad.
- **Interaction** (registered on `#plot3dCanvas`, separate from the 2D `plotSvg`/`window` listeners — 2D's own hover-tooltip listener is explicitly skipped while `plotConfig.type === "3d"`): left-drag rotates (updates `rotY`/`rotX`); middle-click-drag or shift+left-drag pans (`panX`/`panY`, raw pixel delta — no data-domain conversion needed since it's just a screen-space offset); mouse wheel zooms (`plot3dView.zoom`, same `PLOT_ZOOM_WHEEL_FACTOR` as 2D, clamped to `[0.05, 50]`); a "Reset view" button (`#plot3dResetBtn`) restores the default `{rotX:-0.5, rotY:0.7, zoom:1, panX:0, panY:0}`. `#plot2dToolsGroup` (the 2D zoom-%/"Filter from plot view" controls) is hidden for this chart type; `#plotToolbar`'s Fullscreen/Save group stays available. A drag's trailing `click` is suppressed the same way 2D's drag-to-zoom suppresses its own (`plot3dDragMoved` flag, checked and cleared in the `click` handler).
- **Point → log entry**: clicking a point calls the same `revealInTableView` 2D scatter's marks already use. Since canvas has no DOM nodes to hit-test against (unlike SVG's `.plot-mark` circles), hit-testing is nearest-point-within-`PLOT_3D_HOVER_MAX_DIST_PX` against `plotHoverPoints` — the same array 2D's own hover tooltip reads, rebuilt every `renderPlot3D()` call with 3D-shaped entries (`{px, py, rowIndex, xCol, yCol, zCol, colorCol, seriesName}`). The hover tooltip itself reuses `#plotTooltip`/`positionPlotTooltip` unchanged.
- **jsdom/no-canvas-package robustness**: `plot3dCanvas.getContext("2d")` returns `null` in the regression suite's jsdom environment (no `canvas` npm package installed) — `renderPlot3D()` falls back to a no-op stub context (`clearRect`/`fillRect`/`arc`/etc. all no-ops) so every projection/hit-testing computation (`plot3dLastRender`, `plotHoverPoints`) still runs and is testable, just without an actual paint. A real browser always has a working canvas, so this path is dead weight there.

Regression-tested: **Group 125** — axis/color-by/axis-equal-mode/range controls present (and 2D-only controls absent) once the 3D type is picked; the per-axis scale math for all four `axisEqual3d` modes and for manual X/Y/Z range overrides (plus clearing them back to auto) against an asymmetric-range dataset; rotate/zoom/pan mouse interaction (hand-computed against a forced axis-aligned view, since jsdom has no real hit-testing to verify visually); point-click-to-log-entry plus its empty-space and drag-suppression no-ops; and Reset view.

### Plot config persists per extraction node (this session, 2026-08-28, person-requested — *"Die Plots sollen ihren Zustand behalten. Ich möchte einen Plot verlassen und später wieder hineinschauen können und dann den gleichen Plot sehen. Auch wenn ich einen Extraction Knoten kopiere, möchte ich das er den gleichen Plot erzeugt."*)

Previously the whole plot definition — chart type, axes, color-by column, `axisEqual`/`axisEqual3d`, manual ranges — lived in a single shared global (`plotConfig`) that got reset to hardcoded defaults on **every** node switch, including a switch back to the exact same node a moment later: leaving the Plot tab and coming back showed a blank/default plot, not what was there before, and copying an extraction node never carried its plot setup to the copy.

**Now `plotConfig` lives on the node itself** (`node.plotConfig`, an extract-only field, created lazily via `defaultPlotConfig()` the first time a given node's plot is ever configured). The module-level `plotConfig` variable is still what every control/render function reads and mutates — it's just a *reference* to whichever node's config is currently active, swapped in by `loadPlotConfigForNode(node)` (renamed from the old `resetPlotConfig()`), called from `renderExtractTable()` on every genuine node switch (`extractNodeId !== node.id`, or — covering undo/redo restoring a fresh node object under the same id — `plotConfig !== node.plotConfig`). Because objects are references, every in-place edit throughout the controls' change handlers (`plotConfig.xCol = ...` etc.) automatically stays in sync with `node.plotConfig` — there's no separate "save" step to forget.

**What still resets on a node switch**: `plotZoom`/`plot3dView` (the zoom/pan/rotation *viewport*) — a property of "what you're looking at right now," not of the plot's definition, so a fresh look at a node's data reasonably starts from its home view every time, even when that node's own axis/type/range choices are remembered.

**Threaded through all four persistence carriers**, per CLAUDE.md's "any new filter-node field" gotcha:
- `cloneSubtree` (copy/paste) — deep-clones `plotConfig` (`JSON.parse(JSON.stringify(...))`) so a pasted copy starts with the exact same plot but as a fully independent object; editing the copy's plot afterward never leaks back into the original.
- `snapshotSubtree`/`restoreSubtree` (undo/redo) — same deep-clone-on-snapshot, direct-assign-on-restore shape `assertions` already used.
- `serializeFilterBranch`/`importFilterJson` (save/load a filter file) — `importFilterJson` runs the imported value through **`sanitizePlotConfig(raw)`** rather than trusting it directly, since a filter file can be hand-edited or come from anywhere: it rebuilds a safe `defaultPlotConfig()`, copying over only recognized, correctly-typed fields (`type` must be one of the four known chart types, `axisEqual3d` one of the five known modes, `yCols` filtered to actual integers, etc.) — the same "filter to known-good values, default the rest" stance `ignoredColumns`' own import path already takes. A field that fails validation just falls back to its default instead of corrupting the render.
- `serializeFilterTreeForCache`/`materializeCachedFilters` (the IndexedDB session cache, reused by session export/import) — same shape as the file save/load pair above, `materializeCachedFilters` also running incoming values through `sanitizePlotConfig`.

Regression-tested: **Group 126** — the node carries its own `plotConfig` (not just a detached global); leaving the Plot tab (switching to the file's Table view) and returning to the same node shows the exact same plot with no re-selection, verified both on the in-memory `plotConfig` and on the actually-rendered controls (active chart-type button, axis-equal-mode select, manual range input); copying the node via `pasteClipboard()` reproduces the identical plot on the copy, as a genuinely independent deep copy (editing the copy's config afterward doesn't touch the original's); undo restores a deleted node's `plotConfig` alongside the rest of it; the filter save/load JSON round trip and the session-cache serialize/materialize round trip both carry `plotConfig` through intact; and `sanitizePlotConfig` falls back to safe defaults for every field of a deliberately corrupt/foreign imported value (bogus chart type, non-numeric column indices, non-array `yCols`, unknown `axisEqual3d` mode).

### Plot config: inherited at creation, and persisted for a node that only INHERITS the Plot tab (this session, 2026-09-10, person-requested)

**Inherit-at-creation.** `createFilterNode()` now does a one-time deep copy of the parent's `plotConfig`, if it has one, onto every new child node regardless of the child's own `filterType`: `if (parent.plotConfig) node.plotConfig = JSON.parse(JSON.stringify(parent.plotConfig))`. Since `createFilterNode` is the single creation path for every filter type (the text-filter popup, Level, a timerange via the plot's own "Select"/right-click/time-range dialog, Idset, …), this one hook covers all of them — most notably, creating a timerange filter from an already-configured plot's "Select" now starts that new node's own (inherited) plot with the exact same axes/columns/ranges already dialed in, instead of a blank `defaultPlotConfig()` the first time its Plot tab is opened. It's a genuine one-time copy, not a live link: later edits on either node's plot never affect the other, same as `cloneSubtree`'s existing copy/paste behavior for the same field.

**Persistence gap for an inheriting node, found while implementing the above.** A node doesn't need its own extraction pattern to show a Plot tab — `findExtractionAncestor`/`nodeIsExtractionView` (see "filterType merge" above) let a purely-narrowing descendant (timerange, idset, level, context/countContext — anything that only shrinks or context-extends the entry set) inherit Table/Plot from an extraction-pattern ancestor, and such a node gets its own real, independently-configurable `node.plotConfig` (`renderExtractTable`'s own comment: "plotConfig deliberately stay per-`node` — a per-view refinement, not part of the inherited pattern"). But all four persistence carriers gated reading/writing `plotConfig` on `node.filterType === "text"` — which a timerange/idset/... node inheriting the tab never is. So while such a node's plot worked fine live in the session, it silently reverted to a blank plot after **copy/paste** (`cloneSubtree`), a **JSON export/import round trip** (`serializeFilterBranch`/`importFilterJson`), or a **session-cache restore** (`serializeFilterTreeForCache`/`materializeCachedFilters`) — only undo/redo (`snapshotSubtree`/`restoreSubtree`, which never had that gate) was already correct. Fixed by changing the `plotConfig`-specific gate at all four carrier call sites from `filterType === "text"` to `nodeIsExtractionView(node)` — exactly the same predicate that decides whether the node shows a Plot tab in the first place, so "persist plotConfig iff this node can actually show one" is now the one consistent rule. (The identical `filterType === "text"` gate on `assertions`/`columnRenames`/`ignoredColumns` at the same four call sites has the same latent gap and was deliberately left as-is — out of the requested scope, callable out separately if it's ever reported.)

**`yCols` no longer destructively truncated on a chart-type switch.** Switching to Scatter/3D (which show only one Y series) used to overwrite `plotConfig.yCols` in place down to its first entry — switching back to Line/Bar afterward permanently lost the rest of whatever multi-column selection was there before (separately person-reported, same session: *"wenn ich auf einem Plot eine x Achse einstelle, soll der Wert auch in der x Achse stehen wenn ich auf den nächsten Plot Typ wechsel. gleiches für Y..."*, though X/Z/Color/axisEqual/limits already survived a type switch correctly — they live in the same shared `plotConfig` object across all chart types, only `yCols` had this one destructive special case). New `plotConfig.yColsMulti` field: the type-switch handler stashes the full `yCols` there right before truncating (only entering a single-Y type from a multi-Y one), and restores `yCols` from it when switching back to a multi-Y type. Threaded through `defaultPlotConfig()`/`sanitizePlotConfig()` like `yCols` itself — no carrier changes needed beyond that, since it lives inside the same already-threaded `plotConfig` object.

Regression-tested: **Group 197** — a timerange child created under a configured extraction plot inherits an independent one-time copy (edits on either side afterward stay isolated); that timerange node's own `plotConfig` survives `cloneSubtree`, undo/redo, the JSON export/import round trip, and the session-cache round trip (the first three failed before the `nodeIsExtractionView` gate fix); a timerange node with no extraction ancestor still correctly gets and keeps no `plotConfig` at all (no regression for the ordinary non-plotting case); and a Line → Scatter → Line round trip proves the full multi-column Y selection survives instead of collapsing to one column.

### Plot zoom / pan / hover tooltip (this session, 2026-08-18, person-requested)

Mouse-wheel zoom anchored at the cursor, middle-click-drag panning, an editable zoom-level readout (`#plotZoomLevelInput`: +/- buttons, a typed %, Reset — the `−`/field/`+` trio sits inside one shared `.stepper.stepper-compact` pill since this session's UI harmonization, see `docs/ui-and-views.md` → "Shared 'stepper' control"; Reset stays its own separate button beside the pill), left-click-drag rectangle zoom (multi-step), and a hover tooltip showing a mark's exact underlying value — for all three chart types (Line/Bar/Scatter), including Bar's categorical X.

**`#plotToolbar`** is the Plot view's own toolbar — a real row in normal flow at the top of `#plotWrap` (`#plotWrap` is now a column: `#plotToolbar` then `#plotBody`, which holds `#plotControls` + `#plotChartArea` as before), the same pattern `#contextToolbar` already established for the Context view rather than an overlay on the chart. It used to live in the shared extraction toolbar's second row (`.extract-toolbar-row2`, next to the Table/Plot `#extractViewTabs`) as `#plotZoomBar`; moving it into the Plot view itself meant it was no longer coupled to a container also used by the Table tab. **`#extractViewTabs` itself is gone** (this session, `docs/archive/ui-implementation-plan.md`) — Table/Plot switching is now done through the main `#fhTabs` group (see "Unified toolbar: Context/Filtered/Table/Plot" in `docs/ui-and-views.md`), and `switchExtractView(view)` is called from `renderMainView()` based on `fhActiveTab` rather than from a click handler on the old sub-toggle; the function itself, and `#plotToolbar`'s own position inside `#plotWrap`, are otherwise unchanged. Two groups:
- **`#plot2dToolsGroup`** — the zoom controls (`−`/level/`+`/Reset) and the "Create filter from plot view" buttons (below), separated by `.ctx-toolbar-sep`. Hidden via `updatePlotZoomIndicator()` whenever there's no 2D render to act on (`plotLastRender` is `null`) or the chart type is 3D (3D rotates/zooms/pans directly on its own canvas, see below) — same `plotLastRender`-gated show/hide as before, just scoped to this sub-group instead of the whole toolbar.
- A second `.toolbar-group` with **Fullscreen** (`#plotFullscreenBtn`) and **Save** (`#plotSaveImageBtn`), always present regardless of chart type or zoom state.

**Fullscreen** (`openPlotFullscreen`/`closePlotFullscreen`): shows just the chart, nothing else — no controls sidebar, no toolbar, no table. Rather than a second fullscreen-only render path, `#plotChartArea` (the actual `#plotSvg`/`#plot3dCanvas`/`#plotDragRect`/`#plotTooltip` node) is physically moved into `#plotFullscreenOverlay`'s `#plotFullscreenChartHost` on open and back under `#plotBody` on close — reparenting a DOM node keeps every zoom/pan/drag/hover listener already bound to it working unchanged in either place, with no duplicated logic. Nothing extra needs building for the legend: the chart itself always carries axis titles and (for multi-series line/bar) an in-SVG legend (see "Axis titles and in-SVG legend" below), so fullscreen gets both for free, drawn as part of `#plotSvg` itself. Exits via the `×` button or Escape (`closePlotFullscreen()` is called from the app's shared global `Escape` keydown handler).

**Bugfix, same-day follow-up (person-reported): the `×` button worked for a 2D chart but not a 3D one.** The button was `position:absolute` in the corner, overlaid on top of `#plotChartArea` — a *later* sibling in the same stacking context, and CSS resolves two `z-index:auto` positioned siblings by tree order, so `#plotChartArea` painted on top of the button regardless of chart type. This was invisible with a 2D chart only because `#plotSvg`'s hit-testing only covers where something is actually drawn — the corner where the button sits happened to be empty, so clicks fell through to the button beneath. `#plot3dCanvas`, being a normal replaced element, is hit-tested everywhere within its box — including that same empty-looking corner — so it silently swallowed the click before it ever reached the button. Fixed by giving the button its own `#plotFullscreenHeader` flex row above the chart instead of overlaying it: nothing to paint over, in either chart type.

**Save** (`exportPlotImage`): exports exactly what's currently on screen, including whatever zoom/pan is active — `#plotSvg`/`#plot3dCanvas` already reflect that (`renderPlotChart` draws from `plotZoom`), so this just rasterizes whichever one is visible to a PNG download, no separate "current view" bookkeeping needed. The SVG path (`svgToPngDataUrl`) clones the live `#plotSvg` node and inlines each element's own *computed* presentation properties (fill/stroke/font/…, via `inlinePlotSvgComputedStyle`) before serializing: a standalone SVG blob loaded into an `<img>` has no access to this page's own `<style>` rules (`.plot-axis-line` etc. only resolve their `var(--border)` etc. inside the live document), so without inlining the exported PNG would render blank. The 3D path copies `#plot3dCanvas`'s pixels directly. Either way the canvas is first filled with `var(--bg-app)` so the exported PNG matches the current theme instead of coming out transparent.

**Zoom state**: `plotZoom` (`{x0,x1,y0,y1}` in data-domain units, or `null` for "no zoom, show the home view") — genuinely ephemeral viewport state, unlike `plotConfig.xMin`/`normalize`/etc. (which now persist per extraction node, see "Plot config persists per extraction node" below): never threaded through any persistence carrier, reset in `loadPlotConfigForNode()` on every node switch and whenever an axis-shape-changing control fires (chart type, X column, Y column(s)/scatter Y, normalize toggle, a manual X/Y range edit) since a zoom domain computed for the old axis shape is meaningless for the new one.

**"Home" domain and the zoom-out ceiling**: `renderPlotChart` first computes the exact same domain it always did with no zoom (now named `xHomeDomainMin/Max`/`yHomeDomainMin/Max`, post-`axisEqual`-padding) — this is exactly what's shown when `plotZoom` is null (the default view is completely untouched by anything below). `clampZoomAxis(homeLo, homeHi, wantLo, wantHi)`, a small helper nested in `renderPlotChart`, caps the requested span at the home span **plus a small buffer on each side** (`PLOT_ZOOM_OUT_BUFFER = 0.08`, i.e. 8% of the home span per side — bugfix, this session, 2026-08-18, person-reported: a mark sitting exactly on the home view's own edge rendered only half-visible, with the old exact-home clamp giving no way to zoom out or pan even slightly to center it) and keeps the requested position within those same widened bounds (`boundLo/boundHi = homeLo∓buffer .. homeHi±buffer`); zooming IN still has no ceiling — this is "zoom out a *little* past the current default view, zoom in unlimited," the buffer existing purely so an edge mark can be fully centered with some padding around it, not to meaningfully change what "zoomed out" means. The clamped result becomes `xDomainMin/Max`/`yDomainMin/Max`, the actual pixel-mapping domain for that render; ticks/gridlines are recomputed from this *effective* (possibly zoomed) domain every render via a fresh `niceTicks()` call, so grid density stays sensible at any zoom level instead of only ever showing the home view's spacing. Because panning goes through this exact same clamp, the buffer also quietly fixes panning: even at 100% zoom (span == home span) there's now `±buffer` of room to slide the view, where before the position clamp forced `lo === homeLo` exactly whenever `span === homeSpan`, making any pan at the default zoom level a hard no-op.

**Bar charts made zoomable/pannable in X** by generalizing what was previously bespoke `groupW`/row-index arithmetic: a bar chart's raw X domain is simply `[0, rowCount]` (row-index units), fed through `niceTicks`-free but otherwise identical to line/scatter's domain pipeline — `xPix` becomes the single source of truth for row placement (`xPix(rowIndex)`, `xPix(1)-xPix(0)` for the per-row pixel width) instead of `left + groupW*rowIndex` computed directly from `plotW/rowCount`. Zooming into a bar chart's X now shows a subset of rows, wider; the X-tick label loop only walks the row range that overlaps the current domain (`Math.floor(xDomainMin)..Math.ceil(xDomainMax)`) instead of always `0..rowCount`.

**Clipping**: since a zoomed/panned view can legitimately place a point, bar, or line segment outside the plot rectangle (SVG doesn't clip that on its own), all marks render inside a `<g clip-path="url(#plotClip)">` wrapping a `<clipPath>` rect matching the plot area exactly; every legend (the multi-series swatch row, the scatter color-scale strip) renders *after* that group closes, since both sit outside the clip rect's bounds (above/right of it) and would otherwise be invisible.

**Interaction layer** (`plotSvg`/`window` listeners, registered once, reading/writing `plotZoom` and a `plotLastRender` snapshot — geometry + domain written at the end of every `renderPlotChart()` call — so mouse handlers never recompute the chart themselves):
- **Wheel** (`zoomPlotAt(dataX, dataY, factor)`): converts the cursor to data-space via the last render's mapping, proposes a new `plotZoom` scaled around that point (`factor<1` in, `>1` out), ignored when the cursor is outside the plot rectangle. The anchor point is left fixed on screen because the new domain is built symmetrically around it before clamping.
- **Middle-click-drag pan**: rAF-batched exactly like the panel-resizer drag handlers (`plotPanTicking` guard, same shape as `xTicking` elsewhere) — translates the domain by the pixel delta converted to data units, re-clamped every frame by `renderPlotChart` itself, so panning at 100% zoom (home view, no headroom) is naturally a no-op rather than needing a special case.
- **Left-click-drag rectangle zoom** (`PLOT_DRAG_THRESHOLD_PX = 3`, same threshold convention as the timeline minimap's own drag-select): a plain `<div>` overlay (`#plotDragRect`, not SVG — same reasoning as the minimap's drag overlay, a re-render mid-drag would otherwise wipe it) tracks the dragged rectangle in `#plotChartArea`'s own coordinate space; on mouseup, the pixel rect is inverse-mapped to a data-space `{x0,x1,y0,y1}` and set as the new `plotZoom` directly — no extra logic needed for "multi-step" (zooming further into an already-zoomed view), since it's just another absolute domain, clamped the same way. The mouseup's trailing `click` event is swallowed via a one-shot `plotDragSuppressClick` flag, the exact same pattern the minimap's `minimapDragSuppressClick` already established, so a drag never also triggers the mark-click jump-to-log-entry.
- **Zoom-level readout** (`#plotZoomLevelInput`, `updatePlotZoomIndicator()`): shows `round(avg(homeXSpan/curXSpan, homeYSpan/curYSpan) * 100)` as a %, skipped while the field has focus so it doesn't fight active typing. Typing a value (`setPlotZoomLevel`) sets an **absolute** zoom relative to the home span, centered on the current view's own center — not relative to whatever's currently on screen, matching how a zoom-level number is normally read. `+`/`-` buttons call `zoomPlotAt` centered on the current view; Reset sets `plotZoom = null`.
- **Hover tooltip** (`#plotTooltip`, `plotHandleHoverMove`): reads `plotHoverPoints`, one entry per rendered mark rebuilt alongside the marks themselves every render (`{px,py,rowIndex,xCol,yCol,...}` for line/scatter, `{bx,by,bw,bh,...}` for bar). Line/scatter use nearest-point-within-`PLOT_HOVER_MAX_DIST_PX`(14) — their marks are small circles, exact-pixel hit-testing would be too finicky; Bar hit-tests the actual rect bounds directly, since adjacent bars never overlap. The tooltip always looks the value up **live** from `extractRowsData[rowIndex].values[col]` rather than caching a formatted copy, so it shows the real extracted string (the "exact value" requirement) rather than an axis-rounded one. One exception, shared by the 2D and 3D tooltip through `plotTooltipColumnLine`: the time column (`ELAPSED_COL`, "t (ms)") of a log with timestamps (`extractTimeBase != null`) reads as clock time like the X axis does — label "Time", value `HH:mm:ss.SSS` (always with ms), `yyyy-MM-dd ` in front when the extracted rows span midnight; plain text ("Line") and every other column stay raw. **Positioning** (`positionPlotTooltip`, bugfix this session, 2026-08-18, person-reported: a mark far right in the chart pushed the tooltip partly outside `#plotChartArea`, since the old fixed `cursorX + 14`/`cursorY - 28` offset never accounted for the tooltip's own rendered size): the tooltip's `offsetWidth`/`offsetHeight` are measured for real (after `innerHTML`/unhiding, so they're non-zero) and used to prefer above-and-right of the cursor, flipping to below and/or left independently on whichever axis actually lacks room, then clamped a final time to `#plotChartArea`'s own bounds (`PLOT_TOOLTIP_MARGIN = 4`) as a backstop. Placing it above the cursor by default (`PLOT_TOOLTIP_GAP = 12` clearance) is also what keeps the tooltip box itself from ever overlapping the pointer, not just an accident of the old fixed offset.

**Axis titles and in-SVG legend** (person-requested, same session: *"Zeige auch in den 2D Plots eine Legende und Achsbeschriftung, damit man das auch im Fullscreen und Exportierten Bild nachvollziehen kann."*) — 2D charts (line/bar/scatter) now always draw the plotted column *names*, not just numeric tick labels, so a fullscreen view or a saved/exported image is self-explanatory without the sidebar's column pickers next to it. Both are part of `renderPlotChart`'s own SVG output (`.plot-axis-title` text elements, `PLOT_MARGIN` widened — `left` 58→72, `bottom` 38→52 — to fit them), so they're included in fullscreen and the exported PNG automatically, same as everything else drawn there.
