X always gets a title (there's always exactly one X column); Y only when there's exactly one Y series (`series.length === 1`) — with several, a shared Y title couldn't describe them all, and the **existing** per-series legend (swatch + name, drawn at the top of the chart when `series.length > 1` — this predates this session, it just wasn't visible outside the normal Plot tab before axis titles/fullscreen/save existed) already names each one by its own color. Not added for the 3D chart type (out of scope for this request — it draws to a `<canvas>`, not an SVG, and has its own separate render path).

### "Create filter from plot view" (`FEATURE_BACKLOG.md` #11)

**Rewritten 2026-09-07 (person-requested — unify the Table/Plot filters):**
the two dedicated `#plotToolbar` buttons this used to live behind
(`#plotFilterTimeRangeBtn`/`#plotFilterEntriesBtn`) are gone. The Plot
tab's viewport now feeds the same unified row-actions every other tab
uses (see "Filter-Toolbar" in `docs/ui-and-views.md`): **"Time range"**
in `#viewBar` creates a `"timerange"` filter (see `docs/filters.md` →
"Time filters") spanning the viewport's min/max timestamp, and
**"Select"** in `#plotToolbar`'s own Actions group builds a selection
filter (`docs/filters.md` → "Add to selection") from exactly those entries —
covering what the old dedicated "Filter: these entries" `"idset"` button
used to (an `"idset"` filter still exists, and selections are built from
it — see `docs/filters.md`, "Add to selection" — the direct viewport→`"idset"`
button just no longer has its own dedicated trigger). Both key off the
extraction node currently active, resolve their input from whatever's
currently visible in the plot's own zoomed/panned viewport (the home/
un-zoomed domain when no zoom is active, so either with no zoom applied
covers the whole extraction), and are enabled only once something is
actually plotted in 2D (`plot2dToolsAvailable`).

`getPlotViewportEntries()` is the shared "what's on screen right now" primitive: it reads `plotLastRender.xDomainMin`/`xDomainMax`/`yDomainMin`/`yDomainMax` (the last real render's effective, possibly-zoomed domain on both axes) and, for each `extractRowsData` row, derives the same X position `renderPlotChart` itself would place it at — a bar chart's row-index slot center (`r + 0.5`, since bar's X is categorical row-index space, see above) or the X column's `parseValueForPlot`-parsed value for line/scatter — so it can never drift out of sync with what's actually drawn. A row also needs a **Y** check, not just X (bugfix, this session, 2026-08-28, person-reported): a row can have an in-range X but sit above/below the current Y zoom/pan, or have no finite Y at all for any of `plotConfig.yCols` (the same NaN-drop `renderPlotChart`'s own `series` construction applies) — either way it isn't actually drawn, so it's kept only if X is in range **and** at least one selected Y column's parsed value is finite and within the Y domain. A viewport containing fewer than two rows shows a toast and creates no "Time range" filter node (2026-09-07: the threshold moved from "zero rows" to "fewer than two", since "Time range" now needs 2+ entries the same way it does everywhere else — "Select" still only needs one).

Regression-tested: **Group 123** in `tests/philogg.regression.test.js` — the unified "Time range" action under the home view (covers the whole extraction), under a real zoomed viewport (scoped to exactly the visible rows), and the sub-2-entries-viewport no-op case; **Group 183c** covers "Select" building a selection filter from the Plot viewport.

## Value assertions (extraction columns)

Per numeric-capable extraction column (`isPlottableType`: `float`/`int`/`hex`/`time` — same set the Plot tab already offers as axis candidates), an optional expected-value check: either a **range** (min and/or max, either side optional) or a **target ± tolerance**. Stored as `node.assertions = { [colIndex]: { mode: "range"|"target", min, max, target, tolerance } }` on the `extract` node itself — lazily created the first time a column gets one, never on other filter types.

**Checking a value**: `checkAssertion(node, colIndex, rawValue, type)` parses the cell via the same `parseValueForPlot` the Plot tab uses, and returns `true` (violated) / `false` (passed) / `null` (no assertion configured, or the value didn't parse as a number — an unparseable cell is neither a pass nor a violation, same "leave it alone" stance sorting already takes with unparseable values). `assertionSummary(node, colIndex)` scans the current `extractRowsData` once to produce the `{violations, checked, total}` used for the header badge.

**UI**: a **Table toolbar action** (`#tableAssertBtn`, in `#tableToolbar`'s Actions group, target-icon SVG) — not a per-column header button anymore (person-requested, 2026-09-15: the old header button, `.extract-assert-btn`, was too small to notice). Disabled until one or more **whole columns** are currently selected in the extraction table (`assertableSelectedColumns()`, built on the existing cell-selection model — see `getSelectedColumns`/`isColumnFullySelected`); a column is selected the same way it always was, via a plain/Ctrl/Shift header click, only non-plottable columns among the selection are left out. Clicking it opens `#assertDialog` (mirrors the `#contextDialog`/`#linkDialog` small-modal pattern), where Range/Target±Tolerance is a two-button mode toggle rather than a dropdown. Each of the four fields (min/max/target/tolerance) is a shared `.stepper` pill (this session, 2026-09-15's UI harmonization — see `docs/ui-and-views.md` → "Shared 'stepper' control") instead of a bare native number spinner: still a plain typed value (min/max have no lower clamp — a legitimate assertion range can be negative; tolerance is clamped to `min:0`, via `initNumberStepper`'s own `opts.min`), just with a −/+ pair flanking it instead of relying on the browser's own spin buttons. With exactly one assertable column selected, the dialog pre-fills that column's existing assertion (or blank) and labels itself with the column's name — unchanged from before; with 2+ selected, it opens blank (they may already differ from each other) and labels itself "N columns selected" instead, and Save/Clear then apply to **every** selected column in one `withFieldEditUndo` pass — select several columns, open the dialog once, and set the same rule on all of them instead of one dialog per column. Once a column has an assertion, its header still shows the small "N of M outside range" badge — colored via `--level-error` only once `violations > 0` (a configured-but-currently-passing assertion stays quiet, not attention-grabbing) — unaffected by this move, since it was never part of the removed button. Violating cells in the table get `.assert-violation` (a `--level-error-soft` tint + colored text, same visual language as `.log-row.lvl-error`).

**Sort button, same session**: `.extract-sort-btn` (the ▲/▼/⇅ glyph next to a column's name) grew from 10px to 13px, matching the other 13px icon buttons already used throughout the app's toolbars — person-reported it read too small next to the toolbar buttons around it once the assertion button moved there.

**Bugfix, same session (person-reported: "why does the dialog show both range and target/tolerance fields at once when the toggle above is supposed to switch between them?")**: `updateAssertModeUI()` already did `#assertRangeFields`/`#assertTargetFields.classList.toggle("hidden", …)` correctly, but no CSS rule in the whole stylesheet ever targeted `#assertRangeFields.hidden`/`#assertTargetFields.hidden` — this project has no bare `.hidden{display:none}` rule, every one is scoped to its own selector (see the `#viewBar .row-actions.hidden` comment in the CSS), and this pair never got theirs. So the class was toggled correctly but had zero visual effect, and both field groups showed regardless of which mode button was active — the same class of bug Group 70e hit once before (a `.hidden` class with no matching rule). Fixed with a scoped `#assertRangeFields.hidden, #assertTargetFields.hidden{display:none;}` rule. Regression-tested in Group 14 via `isVisible()` (checks real `getComputedStyle` `display`, not just `classList.contains("hidden")`, specifically because that's the class of bug this catches) at both the default Range mode and after switching to Target ± tolerance.

**Plot tab**: a point/bar whose value on *either* axis fails that axis's column's own assertion gets an extra error-colored ring/border drawn on top (line: outlined circle; bar: colored stroke; scatter: larger outlined ring) — on the theory that a plot is often where an out-of-range value actually gets *noticed*, since the table's cell tint is easy to scroll past. The ring color (`PLOT_ASSERT_COLOR`) is a plain hex literal matching `--level-error`, not a CSS custom property — kept consistent with every other plot color (`COLUMN_PALETTE`, `PLOT_COLOR_STOPS`), since the whole chart is built as raw SVG attribute strings in JS, not as CSS-styled elements.

**Persistence**: assertions travel with the node through `serializeFilterBranch`/`importFilterJson` (filter save/load JSON) and `cloneSubtree` (copy/paste), the same way `inverted`/`bakedA`/`contextBefore` etc. do — an assertion is part of what makes an extraction "the same filter," not a transient view setting. They are **not** reset when the extraction pattern is edited to add/remove columns; a stale assertion on a column index that no longer means what it used to is a known sharp edge (see Known limitations). `node.ignoredColumns` (see "Extraction: live pattern preview + ignored columns" below) follows this exact same 4-touch-point precedent (plus `snapshotSubtree`/`restoreSubtree` for undo/redo, which assertions also already went through).

## Statistics panel

Min / max / mean / stddev per numeric-capable extraction column (`computeColumnStats`), rendered in a standalone `#statsPanel` (`renderStatsBar` writes the chips into its `#extractStatsContent`) — hidden entirely (`.stats-empty`, showing `#statsPanelEmpty` instead) when no column is numeric. Single pass to collect values + running min/max/sum, second pass for the variance sum — two passes over `extractRowsData`, not `Math.min/max(...spread)`, specifically to avoid the call-stack argument-count ceiling some engines hit on very large arrays (extraction results are already documented as "not virtualized — fine for realistically-sized results," so this stays in that same performance envelope rather than trying to be smarter). The plots, the time-range actions and the table's column selection avoid the same ceiling through the shared `arrayMin`/`arrayMax` loop helpers (top of the main script; 2026-10-02, GROUP big-array-spread). Numbers are formatted with the Plot tab's existing `formatAxisNumber` (nice/short representation) rather than a separate formatter.

**Table-only, positioned/behaving like Entry Detail** (person-requested, 2026-09-05 — replaces an earlier per-tab collapse-toggle design the same session): `#statsPanel` sits at the bottom of `#extractWrap`'s own flex column, below `#extractScroll`/`#plotWrap`, with the exact same collapsed/peeking pin-or-hover mechanism as `#detailPanel` (`isStatsCollapsed`/`isStatsPeeking`/`toggleStatsCollapsed`, modeled directly on their `#detailPanel` counterparts; the same `hoverExpandDetail` Setting governs both panels' hover-peek). Unlike Entry Detail, it defaults **pinned open** (`localStorage["philogg-stats-collapsed"]` unset = expanded) and has no manual drag-resizer (a fixed height is enough for a handful of stat chips). `switchExtractView()` shows the panel only while Table is the active sub-view (`statsPanel.style.display`) — Plot has no Statistics panel at all anymore, and neither view's own toolbar carries a Statistics toggle button any longer; the panel's own header toggle (`#statsToggle`) is the only control.

## Extraction: live pattern preview + ignored columns

From person-supplied `REQUIREMENTS-extract-preview-and-ignore.md`: two related gaps in the extraction workflow — no preview of what a pattern actually captures *while typing it* (only an after-the-fact match count), and no way to have a placeholder anchor the pattern without becoming a permanent column.

### Ignored columns — data model (Option B)

**Option B chosen** over the doc's alternative ("a new `[ignore]` pattern token"): `node.ignoredColumns: number[]` — indices into the compiled pattern's columns — on the extraction-capable `"text"` node itself (see "filterType merge" further down — there is no separate `"extract"` filterType anymore), lazily created the first time a column gets ignored, same convention as `node.assertions`. Chosen because it's the smaller, self-contained change the doc itself flagged as the likely winner: the regex/matching is **completely untouched** (an ignored placeholder still anchors the pattern exactly as before), it's a pure display/export-time filter, and it doesn't need to decide how a new token interacts with column auto-naming (`value`, `value 2`, ...) the way a `[ignore]` token would. `isColumnIgnored(node, colIndex)` / `setColumnIgnored(node, colIndex, ignored)` are the two small helpers everything else goes through.

**A structural consequence worth understanding before touching extraction code again**: `extractColumns` (the module-level global) is no longer a dense, positional array — it's the *currently visible* subset of the compiled pattern's columns, and it can have gaps. Each surviving element keeps its original compiled-pattern position as a stable `.colIndex` property (this is the number `node.ignoredColumns` contains, the number `data-col`/`data-sort-col`/`data-assert-col` DOM attributes carry, and the number `node.assertions`/`plotConfig.xCol`/`.yCols`/`.colorCol`/`extractSortCol` are keyed by) — while `row.values` in each `extractRowsData` entry stays the **full, unfiltered** array (one value per compiled column, ignored or not), since matching itself never changes. `findExtractColumn(colIndex)` resolves a stable `colIndex` back to its (visible) descriptor, returning `null` when that column is currently ignored — every colIndex-keyed lookup (`computeColumnStats`, `assertionSummary`, `openAssertDialog`, `extractRowComparator`, the Plot tab's axis-candidate derivation) goes through it rather than bracket-indexing `extractColumns` directly. The cell-selection subsystem (`rowCells`/`rangeCells`/`columnsRangeCells`/`allCells`) was adjusted the same way — it walks `extractColumns`' actual `.colIndex` values instead of assuming a dense `0..length-1` range, so a shift-click column-range spanning an ignored column simply skips it rather than silently selecting hidden data.

**Excluded from**, per the requirements doc's list — all confirmed by Group 24's regression coverage: the extraction table (`renderExtractTable` never emits a `<th>`/`<td>` for an ignored column), column statistics (`computeColumnStats` returns `null` for one), the Plot tab's axis-candidate list (an ignored column is simply absent from `extractColumns`, so the existing `plottable` derivation — and its already-existing stale-selection reconciliation for `plotConfig.xCol`/`.yCols`, originally built for pattern edits — transparently also handles a column being ignored/un-ignored, no extra code needed there), whole-table CSV export (`buildExtractCsv` maps through each *visible* column's `.colIndex` rather than joining `row.values` wholesale; the Ctrl+C cell-range copy needed no change at all, since the cell-selection generators above already never produce a selection cell for an ignored column). Value assertions: an ignored column gets no assert button (no `<th>` at all), but — same accepted sharp edge as assertions surviving a pattern edit — an assertion configured *before* a column was ignored is left in `node.assertions` untouched, not deleted; it simply stops being checked/shown while the column stays ignored (`assertionSummary`/`computeColumnStats` both return `null` via `findExtractColumn`).

**Two toggle surfaces**, both wired to the same `setColumnIgnored`:
- **Post-creation**, in the existing `#extractPatternView` (the colored-chip template view above the table): `renderExtractPatternView` gained an optional third `opts` argument, `{ onToggle(colIndex) }` — when present, every chip becomes clickable (`.chip-toggleable`) and dimmed (`.chip-ignored`) when ignored, `title` reflecting the current state. `renderExtractTable` passes the **full, unfiltered** column list here (re-derived from `spec.columns` — NOT the filtered `extractColumns` — since this function independently re-walks every raw placeholder token in the pattern text and must produce exactly one chip per token regardless of ignore state) plus an `onToggle` that calls `setColumnIgnored`/`renderExtractTable` directly on the live node.
- **While authoring**, in the new `#filterPopup` preview (see below) — clicking a highlighted span toggles a *popup-local* working set, `filterPopupIgnored` (a `Set`, module-level `let`), applied to the node only on submit. Pre-populated from the edited node's existing `ignoredColumns` in edit mode (`openEditFilterPopup`), empty in create mode, cleared on close — so a filter can be created with columns already marked ignored, and re-opening Edit shows the current state immediately. `createFilterNode`/`updateFilterNode` both gained a 5th optional `ignoredColumns` parameter for this (backward compatible — every other existing call site is unaffected).

### Renamed columns (this session, 2026-09-02, person-requested)

`node.columnRenames: { [colIndex]: string }` — a display-name override, keyed by the same stable `colIndex` `ignoredColumns`/`assertions` use, lazily created the first time a column gets renamed (same convention as both). Unlike a `[ignore]` token, this is purely cosmetic: the compiled pattern's own token name (`spec.columns[i].name`, or the literal `"Index"`/`"t (ms)"` for the two synthetic columns) is completely untouched — a rename only changes what's *shown*. `getColumnDisplayName(node, colIndex, compiledName)` / `renameColumn(node, colIndex, name)` are the two small helpers everything else goes through (renaming to blank/whitespace clears the override, reverting to the compiled name); `renderExtractTable` applies the overlay once, right after `extractColumns`/`patternColumns` are (re)built from the compiled pattern, so every consumer downstream — the table header, `#extractPatternView`'s chip tooltip, `findExtractColumn` (and through it the Plot tab's axis titles/legend, column stats, assertions) — sees the renamed name for free, with no per-consumer awareness needed.

**UI**: right-click a column header → "Rename column…" (`#ctxRenameColumn`, only shown in `#extractContextMenu` when the right-click actually landed on a `th[data-col]` — `extractContextMenuColIndex` records which), or **F2** while exactly one column is selected (a plain, non-Ctrl/Shift click on its header — `getSingleSelectedColumn()` checks `state.tableSelection` is exactly that column's own `columnCells`, nothing more/less). Either swaps the header's name for a `.extract-col-rename-input` text box (`renamingColIndex`, part of `renderExtractTable`'s own header-building loop — the same string-based `<th>` construction, not a separate DOM-node path) — Enter commits, Escape cancels, blur commits (mirrors the tree's own `startRenameNode`/`renderRenameInput`, just rebuilt for a string-templated header instead of DOM nodes). F2 checks the column-selection case *first*; with nothing/more than one column selected it falls through to the existing tree-node rename (`startRenameNode`), so the shortcut keeps its original meaning everywhere else.

**Persistence**: threaded through every carrier `node.assertions` already established — `cloneSubtree`, `captureNodeFields`/`applyNodeFields` (undo/redo edits), `snapshotSubtree`/`restoreSubtree` (undo/redo add/delete), `serializeFilterBranch`/`importFilterJson` (save/load), `serializeFilterTreeForCache`/`materializeCachedFilters` (session cache). Import sanitizes via `sanitizeColumnRenames` (same "filter to known-good values, drop the rest" stance `sanitizePlotConfig` already takes) — a non-integer key, a non-string value, or an all-whitespace name are all dropped individually rather than rejecting the whole map.

**Fixed bug (2026-09-04): renaming was impossible while the underlying file was being tailed.** `renderExtractTable` used to unconditionally rebuild `extractHead.innerHTML`, including on the re-renders `onTailChange`/`tailTick` trigger for every new chunk of a live-tailed file — that detaches the focused `.extract-col-rename-input`, which fires a synchronous `blur` and thus commits/cancels the rename before the user typed anything. `renderExtractTable` now checks upfront whether `document.activeElement` is the live rename input for `renamingColIndex` and, if so, skips the header rebuild entirely (row data below still refreshes normally); the input keeps focus/caret/value until the user actually commits or cancels.

Regression-tested: **Group 157** — F2 with/without a single column selected, the right-click menu (shown only on a header, not a body right-click), commit/cancel/blank-clears, the renamed name showing in the table header/pattern chip tooltip/Plot axis title, all five persistence carriers (including the import sanitizer dropping a deliberately dirty rename map while keeping the one valid entry in it), and a re-render landing mid-edit (standing in for a tail tick) leaving the focused input and its in-progress value untouched.

### Live pattern preview (`#filterPatternPreview`, in `#filterPopup`)

While typing/editing a pattern, `evaluateLiveMatch`'s existing 150ms debounce now also calls `updateFilterPatternPreview(val, baseEntries)` (one shared timer, not a second competing debounce) — it finds the *first* of `baseEntries` (the same rows `evaluateLiveMatch`'s match-count already uses) the compiled pattern actually matches, and renders that real message with each capture group's substring wrapped in a `<span>` colored via the same `columnColor`/`COLUMN_PALETTE` scheme the table and post-creation pattern view use, so colors stay visually consistent across all three. `white-space:pre-wrap` (matching `#detailMessage`'s own handling) so a multi-line stack-trace sample renders faithfully. Exact per-group `[start,end]` offsets come from a **second** `RegExp` built from `spec.regexStr` with the `d` (match-indices) flag (`m.indices[i+1]`) — the compiled `regex` actually used for matching is untouched, this is purely a preview-time convenience. No matching sample yet → a muted "No matching sample message yet." note (same spirit as the live-match count's `--warn` "0 of N" state, just phrased for a single-message preview). Hidden entirely for a non-extraction (plain text) filter or an invalid pattern.

**Gotcha hit and fixed**: the preview span's click handler must call `ev.stopPropagation()`. Without it, clicking a span — whose handler synchronously does `filterPatternPreview.innerHTML = ""` to re-render — detaches the clicked span from the DOM *while the click event is still bubbling*. The existing global "click outside a popup closes it" handler (`document`'s click listener, `!filterPopup.contains(ev.target) && ...`) then sees a detached `ev.target`, `contains()` correctly returns `false` for it, and the popup closes itself out from under the click. The post-creation pattern-chip toggle already had this same guard for the identical reason (a chip click re-renders the whole `#extractPatternView`); this is the second instance of the same class of bug, worth remembering for any future click handler that re-renders its own clicked ancestor. **A third instance turned up in the very next session** (person-reported): `treeContextMenu`'s click handler — right-click → "Edit filter…" opened `#filterPopup`, then the still-bubbling click reached the same global handler and closed it right back, since `closeTreeContextMenu()` only toggles a class rather than removing the menu item, so `ev.target` was simply *outside* `#filterPopup` this time rather than detached — same root cause (a click that opens something else must not keep bubbling to a close-on-outside-click listener), different trigger. Fixed the same way; see "Status / changelog" for the bugfix-session entry.

### Testing note

The person-supplied companion `tests/extract-preview-ignore.spec.js` is kept as a standalone file (its own acceptance criteria call for that — a BASELINE group pinning today's "every placeholder is a column" behavior, and a CONDITIONAL group that self-skips until `node.ignoredColumns`/`setColumnIgnored` exists, then activates automatically) — but, following this project's established convention (see README.md "Extending this suite", and the same choice made for `link-chaining.spec.js` in Group 22), the **primary** coverage lives in `tests/philogg.regression.test.js` as **Group 24**: the popup preview's span rendering/toggle/submit flow, edit-mode pre-population, the post-creation chip toggle, exclusion from table/stats/assertions/plot/export, and persistence through all four of `cloneSubtree`/undo-redo/save-load/session-cache (session export/import gets this for free, since it reuses the session-cache serialization functions).


## Extraction workflow: live match feedback & token chips

- **Live match count** (`#filterLiveMatch`, `evaluateLiveMatch()`): debounced (150ms) re-evaluation of whatever's currently typed in `#filterInput`, run against the rows the new filter would apply to, shown as the popup's live result summary — big count, "matches in N", for an extraction pattern a "captures: …" line, a match histogram and three sample rows (see `docs/filters.md` → "Live result summary"). An invalid pattern shows "Invalid pattern" in the `--level-error` color. Zero matches gets a `--warn`-colored nudge rather than an error, since "the pattern is fine but nothing matches yet" is a normal mid-typing state, not a failure.
- **Live pattern preview** (`#filterPatternPreview`, `updateFilterPatternPreview()`, same debounce as the live match count above): for an extraction pattern, shows the pattern evaluated against a real sample message with matched substrings highlighted in place — see "Extraction: live pattern preview + ignored columns" below for the full writeup, including how this doubles as the ignore-toggle UI while authoring.
- **Token chips** (`#filterTokenChips`, one button per placeholder type, now grouped directly under `#filterInput` in the popup's input section — see "Filter popup" above): clicking inserts the literal token (`[*:float]`, `[*:int]`, `[*:time]`, `[*:word]`, `[*:hex]`, or `[*]`) at the current cursor position in `#filterInput` (`insertTokenAtCursor`), replacing any active text selection, same as normal typing would. (The old `#filterHint` plain-text fallback row listing the same placeholders was removed — the chips already insert them directly, making the text redundant.)
- **Extraction table column sort** (`.extract-sort-btn`, one small button inside each `<th>`): sorts `extractRowsData` itself — numeric-capable types (`float`/`int`/`hex`/`time`) numerically via the same `parseValueForPlot` the Plot tab uses, `word` lexically via `localeCompare`, unparseable values always last regardless of direction. The sort button is a separate nested control with its own `mousedown`/`click` handlers (`stopPropagation`) specifically so it doesn't trigger the header's existing mousedown-driven column cell-selection — the two interactions share the same `<th>` but are otherwise independent. **Because the sort reorders `extractRowsData` in place** (rather than keeping a separate display-order array), it also reorders the connected **Plot tab's line-chart point order** for that extraction, since line/bar plotting reads points in row order by design (see Plotting section above) — this was accepted as a reasonable trade-off over the bookkeeping risk of two parallel orderings that could drift out of sync. Sorting also clears any active cell selection in the table (`state.tableSelection = null`), since a positional "row,col" selection would otherwise silently point at different rows post-sort. Sort state resets whenever the active extraction node changes.
